title: Emergency fire pump — click / no crank
scope: Conventional 12/24 V DC starter systems only. Not a crank-but-no-fire flow.

sources.text: Client reported three flat batteries in three days; starter clicked and became hot. Technician reported charger good, no external fault, engine free by hand, intermittent bench spinning and internal burning. Starter replaced; engine started. No measured voltages recorded.
Generic starting-system sequence and less than 0.5 V total main-cable cranking voltage drop. Not an OEM specification for this pump.

safety: Authorised fire-system impairment is in place, responsible site person informed, and alternate fire protection arranged. No active fire demand.
Competent authorised technician; OEM manual and safe test access available. Automatic/remote starting inhibited under site procedure.
PPE and ventilation in place; rotating parts clear; no fuel leak, smoke, hot/bulging battery, damaged cable or hot starter.
Battery arrangement and rated system voltage positively identified. No bridging terminals, bypassing interlocks or improvised bench tests.
stopText: STOP: cease attempts; make safe under site procedure; notify responsible site person. Resolve the hazard or obtain OEM information before a fresh session. Never leave fire protection impaired without the responsible person’s control.

classify.title: Confirm the symptom
classify.instruction: Record asset/model, rated voltage, battery arrangement and observed symptom. If starter is hot, stop and allow cooling per OEM procedure before diagnosis.

choices.label: Click / no crank or intermittent crank
Cranks normally but will not fire
Smoke, heat, unexpected movement or unknown voltage

battery.title: Test batteries first
battery.instruction: Inspect and test EACH battery using its chemistry, rating, temperature and manufacturer load-test procedure. Record rested voltage, loaded voltage, rating, test method and pass/fail. Charger indication alone does not prove battery health. OEM limits unknown: do not invent 12/24 V acceptance thresholds.

choices.label: All batteries pass documented test
Any battery fails
Cannot verify safely / limits unavailable

batteryFix.title: Battery fault requires correction
batteryFix.instruction: Charge/replace failed batteries and correct connections under approved procedure. Repeated discharge still needs charger/parasitic-load investigation. Restart this flow with tested batteries; do not condemn starter from clicking alone.

cables.title: Measure loaded cable voltage drop
cables.instruction: Identify terminals from OEM documentation, not colour. During an authorised brief start attempt within OEM duty cycle: positive drop = battery-pack positive POST to starter B+; negative drop = starter OEM ground point to pack negative POST. Record both V and sum under comparable load. A zero reading with no current is inconclusive. Generic Delco reference: total <0.5 V; use pump/OEM specification where available. Not a universal 24 V limit.

choices.label: Passes applicable documented limit under load
Excessive drop
No meaningful load / unknown terminals or limit

cableFix.title: Repair the supply path
cableFix.instruction: Isolate all relevant power sources per OEM procedure. Inspect/repair loose, damaged or corroded cables and grounds. Restore safe test state, then restart and repeat loaded tests. Do not replace starter before confirming supply.

control.title: Check start command
control.instruction: With OEM wiring and safe access, measure the documented starter command terminal relative to its specified return during START. Record terminal identifier, measured V and OEM required range. Pins, colours and acceptance voltage are unknown in this pack. Do not bridge the solenoid or defeat controller interlocks.

choices.label: Command and starter supply meet OEM requirements
Command missing or outside OEM limits
No diagram / unsafe / cannot establish specification

controlFix.title: Control circuit requires OEM diagnosis
controlFix.instruction: Stop this starter flow. Trace documented controller output, protection and connections under approved fire-pump procedure. No guessed fuse, relay or pin assignments are supplied.

mechanical.title: Rule out mechanical lock safely
mechanical.instruction: Isolate automatic start, charger and all battery sources under OEM/site procedure; verify safe state. Only use the OEM barring method if trained and authorised; never use a fan blade. Record whether engine rotates normally. Starter removal and assessment are qualified-workshop tasks.

choices.label: Engine rotates normally by approved method
Engine locked / abnormal resistance
Unable to verify safely

mechanicalStop.title: Mechanical STOP
mechanicalStop.instruction: Do not crank or force engine. Escalate engine/pump mechanical inspection; a locked load can overheat a healthy starter.

starter.title: Starter suspect — seek independent confirmation
starter.instruction: Supply, command and free engine support starter investigation, not automatic replacement. Isolate before removal. Have a qualified workshop perform the correct secured load/bench assessment to starter-maker specification. Record report and part identity. Free spinning alone does not prove loaded performance.

choices.label: Workshop confirms internal starter fault
Pass / inconclusive / no report

repair.title: Repair and prove operation
repair.instruction: Fit correct rated replacement under OEM procedure; record part and torque source. Reassemble guards and connections. Restore approved test state and run controller/manual-start and automatic-start acceptance tests with responsible personnel; check charger recovery and subsequent battery condition. Record results. Starting once does not resolve recurrent discharge or certify fire-system readiness.

choices.label: All required acceptance tests pass; responsible person accepts handback
Starts but acceptance/discharge checks incomplete
Still fails / new hazard

complete.title: Diagnostic case complete — handback recorded
complete.instruction: Record responsible person, date and acceptance-test reference. Technician/site authority alone authorises return to service; this app issues no certification. Historical case: replacement restored starting, but discharge follow-up was not documented.

pending.title: Repair observed — handback pending
pending.instruction: Keep site impairment management active. Complete outstanding automatic-start, charger/battery and site acceptance checks before authorised handback.

unresolved.title: Unresolved — do not guess
unresolved.instruction: Record evidence and escalate to OEM/workshop. Do not label a starter faulty without supporting assessment.

outside.title: Outside this MVP
outside.instruction: Normal cranking requires a separate fuel/control/engine diagnostic flow. Record symptom and obtain the correct OEM procedure.

stop.title: STOP
stop.instruction: STOP: cease attempts; make safe under site procedure; notify responsible site person. Resolve the hazard or obtain OEM information before a fresh session. Never leave fire protection impaired without the responsible person’s control.
